episode_title: #148 Why AI Could Expand the ESCO Market, Not Just Speed It Up

real_qa.q: What does Upgrade's platform do for Energy Service Companies in the ESCO market?
real_qa.r: Upgrade is an intelligence platform for the built environment that pipes in multiple data sources including satellites, permitting databases, soil conductivity, weather, and solar irradiance to provide high-fidelity predictions about buildings—including HVAC systems, thermal envelope properties, EUI, and efficiency opportunities with payback periods. ESCOs use this to target buildings that need their upgrades, prepare sales conversations with day-one portfolio understanding, accelerate feasibility work by uploading utility data and photos to auto-update energy models, and generate proposal documents for meetings.
real_qa.requete: Upgrade platform ESCO energy service companies

real_qa.q: How will AI and technology tools change the economics of the ESCO market?
real_qa.r: AI tools like Upgrade will compress pre-sale costs, shorten sales timelines, and enable more efficient meetings between buyers and sellers without extensive on-site work and feasibility studies. This allows ESCOs to handle higher volume with more qualified leads, changing the fundamental economics of an industry where a huge share of costs currently happens in pre-feasibility and sales work before contracts are signed.
real_qa.requete: AI ESCO market economics sales efficiency

real_qa.q: Why does the ESCO industry have significant growth potential beyond market share competition?
real_qa.r: The deferred maintenance backlog in the municipal sector is growing, and energy constraints and demands are putting a premium on efficiency. Most macro forces point to tailwinds in this market, so the industry should adopt a growth mentality rather than zero-sum thinking about market share, since there will be more work than any single ESCO can handle.
real_qa.requete: ESCO market growth deferred maintenance backlog

real_qa.q: What are the key differences McKinsey looked for when hiring candidates?
real_qa.r: McKinsey interviewers looked for candidates who were interesting and had pursued non-obvious paths beyond straight consulting club recruitment, and critically, candidates who got genuinely excited about solving the problem itself rather than just trying to get hired. These candidates would 'nerd out' on the business case problem and generate creative ideas, making them colleagues worth hiring.

real_qa.q: How does Brody Boland's early work at ISEC nonprofit inform his approach to sustainability?
real_qa.r: Boland spent three years leading ISEC, a nonprofit focused on cross-cultural understanding and youth development, during which he traveled globally and developed personal connections to communities affected by major events like the 2004 Asian tsunami. These experiences made the world feel smaller and awakened in him a desire to make a positive difference, which drove his focus on sustainability and helping from an environmental perspective throughout his career.
real_qa.requete: Brody Boland ISEC nonprofit sustainability background

real_qa.q: Why does Upgrade build its own custom energy modeling instead of using frontier AI models?
real_qa.r: Upgrade built its own building energy models custom-built for the ESCO purpose because this approach is more accurate than what large frontier models can do. Custom modeling allows Upgrade to provide precise predictions and is particularly important since models are less accurate for facilities with significant process loads like major industrial manufacturing.
real_qa.requete: Upgrade custom energy modeling frontier AI models accuracy

guest.bio_context: Brody Boland grew up in Calgary, Canada, and left his undergraduate degree halfway through to lead a global nonprofit organization called ISEC focused on cross-cultural understanding and youth development for three years, traveling extensively. He subsequently completed his undergraduate degree, joined McKinsey & Company where he spent approximately 15 years (initially a couple of years, then grad school, then 13 years after), and spent 5-10 of those years building McKinsey's real assets practice focused on sustainability and energy for institutional investors, private equity funds, and major building owners, helping decarbonize tens of thousands of buildings.
